name: alpenglow_vote
description: An Alpenglow consensus vote we received from a peer or cast ourselves (see our_vote). Unparseable votes are not included. The row timestamp is when we received the vote, or cast it if our_vote; the *_time columns are the phases that followed, each running until the next, ending at done_time. References: Table 6, Definition 12, Algorithm 1, Lemma 48

slot.description: Which slot the vote is for.

block_id.description: Which block the vote is for (only for notar and notar_fallback, all zeros otherwise).

voter_rank.description: Where the voter ranks in the slot's epoch (only if ranked, 65535 otherwise). Also marks their position in the Cert array

voter_identity.description: Validator identity of the voter, looked up from voter_rank in the slot's epoch (all zeros if voter_rank is 65535).

kind.description: What kind of vote is this.

notar.description: Cast on the slot's first block once its parent is ready at a window start, or once we notarized its parent in the previous slot (Algorithm 2, Definition 15).

final.description: Cast once the block we notarized has a notarization cert and we cast no skip or fallback vote in the slot (Algorithm 2, Definition 18). Names only the slot.

skip.description: Cast for every unvoted slot of the leader window on timeout (Definition 17), on SafeToNotar or SafeToSkip (Algorithm 1), a dead block or the crashed-leader timer. Names only the slot.

notar_fallback.description: Cast on SafeToNotar. At most three per slot (Definition 12).

skip_fallback.description: Cast on SafeToSkip. Names only the slot.

received_from_ip.description: IPv4 address of the peer we received the vote from; ourselves if our_vote, stored as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (all zeros if unknown).

received_from_identity.description: Validator identity of the peer we received the vote from (determined from the QUIC client-side TLS certificate); ourselves if our_vote (all zeros if unknown_peer). Not necessarily the voter; see voter_identity.

our_vote.description: Whether this is our own vote, which we store like any other; received_from_identity is then our identity.

broadcast_reason.description: Why we cast the vote, based on the Alpenglow voting algorithm (not_broadcasted if it is not ours). References: Algorithms 1 and 2, Definitions 15, 16 and 17.

not_broadcasted.description: Not our vote, so we did not broadcast it; see our_vote.

block_replayed.description: Replay completed the block normally, so we vote notar for it.

block_dead.description: Replay ruled the block dead, so we vote skip on the entire rest of the window containing this slot.

parent_ready.description: We hold the certs that make a block a valid parent for the leader window starting at this slot (a notar, notar-fallback or fast-final cert for it, or it is finalized, and skip certs for every slot in between), so we vote notar for the window's first block we held pending.

block_notarized.description: We hold a notar cert for the block we voted notar for and cast no skip or fallback vote in the slot, so we vote final for it.

timeout.description: The slot's timeout fired with no vote cast in it, so we vote skip on the entire rest of the window containing this slot.

timeout_crashed_leader.description: The window's crashed-leader timeout fired with no shred and no vote for its first slot, so we vote skip on every slot of the window.

safe_to_notar.description: No block but this one can be fast-finalized in the slot: notar votes for it reach 40% of stake, or 20% with skip votes bringing the total to 60%, and its parent is notar-fallback certified (Definition 16). Having voted skip or notar for another block in the slot, we vote notar-fallback for it and skip every unvoted slot of the window.

safe_to_skip.description: No block can be fast-finalized in the slot: skip votes plus notar votes for every block but the most-voted one reach 40% of stake (Definition 16). Having voted notar in the slot, we vote skip-fallback for it and skip every unvoted slot of the window.

broadcast_to.description: Who we sent the vote to, by rank like voters: identity and address at each rank, all zeros where we did not send (only if our_vote, empty otherwise).

identity.description: Validator identity of the peer (all zeros if not sent).

ip.description: IPv4 address of the peer as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (all zeros if not sent).

port.description: Port of the peer's Alpenglow QUIC endpoint (0 if not sent).

processing_result.description: What we did with the vote. unknown_peer and banned_peer are decided on the connection before the vote is decoded, shred_version_mismatch and unranked_peer after decoding, in that order; the rest are Alpenglow-specific validation.

unknown_peer.description: The connection had no known peer: we cleared its identity while closing it, or accepted it before we knew the epoch's validators.

banned_peer.description: The peer is banned for an earlier invalid signature or cert; connection closed.

shred_version_mismatch.description: Signed under a different shred version than ours.

unranked_peer.description: The peer has no rank in the slot's epoch.

slot_too_old.description: The slot is more than eight slots behind our finality frontier, or in an earlier epoch we have no stake information for.

slot_too_new.description: The slot is beyond our look-ahead window, or in an epoch we have no stake information for.

slashable.description: Conflicts with a vote the peer already cast for the slot (Lemma 22, Definition 12).

duplicate.description: We already stored this vote or one that covers it: notar and notar-fallback for one block, skip and skip-fallback (Definition 12); ignored.

ignored_redundant.description: We already hold a valid cert for the slot, or block, this vote would count toward; ignored.

accepted.description: Vote is accepted and next step is to aggregate (and broadcast, if our_vote).

quorum_reached_safe_to_notar.description: Notar votes for block_id reached 40% of stake, or 20% with skip votes bringing the total to 60% (Definition 16). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

quorum_reached_safe_to_skip.description: Skip votes plus notar votes for every block but the most-voted one reached 40% of stake (Definition 16). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

quorum_reached_final_cert.description: Final votes for the slot reached 60% of stake (Table 6). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

quorum_reached_fast_final_cert.description: Notar votes for block_id reached 80% of stake (Table 6). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

quorum_reached_notar_cert.description: Notar votes for block_id reached 60% of stake (Table 6). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

quorum_reached_notar_fallback_cert.description: Notar and notar-fallback votes for block_id reached 60% of stake (Table 6). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

quorum_reached_skip_cert.description: Skip and skip-fallback votes for the slot reached 60% of stake (Table 6). Crossing a quorum triggers BLS verification of the votes (see verify_start_time).

aggregation_start_time.description: When we started aggregating the vote into the running BLS aggregate for its slot, kind and block (only if processing_result is accepted, 0 otherwise).

verify_start_time.description: When we started BLS verifying the aggregate this vote completed (only if this vote brought a tally to a quorum of Table 6 or Definition 16, which is when we verify signatures, 0 otherwise).

broadcast_start_time.description: When we started broadcasting the vote to our peers (only if our_vote, 0 otherwise).

done_time.description: When we finished processing the vote, may be any of the above stages including short-circuiting at earlier stages.
